newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso shrugs off gov't plan, ends a tad down.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso shrugs off gov't plan, ends a tad down.

text.p: Mexico's benchmark 48-hour peso reversed an upward trend in early Tuesday trade to end slightly off, as toward the close national banks swapped dollar positions among themselves, dealers said.

The peso's fall came despite the widespread favorable reaction to President Ernesto Zedillo's unveiling of the National Program To Finance Development, traders said. In contrast, Mexican stocks gained strongly.
The spot 48-hour contract ended down 0.65 centavo at 7.9180/7.9230 per dollar. Its 24-hour stablemate closed off 0.6 centavo at 7.9160/7.9190 per dollar.
Earlier in the day, Zedillo unveiled a plan that targets economic growth of an average five percent annually through 2000 and seeks to boost domestic savings.

"Dealers pushed the peso higher in the morning session hoping to trigger a surge of peso demand, and when it did not come, they sold positions among themselves in thin volume," one trader said, adding trading ranges were tight.

Contracts also shrugged off an expected rise in primary interest rates in the government's weekly securities auction. "The market has already discounted any (domestic) rate hikes," argued one peso dealer.
Mexico's same-day peso closed earlier in the session with a rise of one centavo to 7.9035/7.9060 per dollar.
